EXT. LIGHTHOUSE - NIGHT

Waves hammer the rocks. At the top of the old lighthouse, the lamp flickers, dies, and flickers again.

MARA (60s), wrapped in a yellow raincoat, climbs the last steps with a toolbox and a thermos of coffee.

MARA

(to the lamp)

Not tonight. You are not quitting on me tonight.

INT. LAMP ROOM - CONTINUOUS

Mara opens the toolbox. Inside, next to the wrenches, a faded photograph: a much younger Mara and a boy, both grinning at the camera.

The radio on the wall crackles to life.

LEO (V.O.)

Harbor to lighthouse. Mara, are you there? There's a boat out past the reef and they can't see a thing.

MARA

Give me two minutes, Leo. Just two.

She tightens a bolt, wipes the glass with her sleeve and throws the switch. The beam sweeps across the black water.

CUT TO:

EXT. FISHING BOAT - CONTINUOUS

A young sailor squints into the rain, then points at the light.

SAILOR

There! Hard to port!
